Read a set of scenarios from a manifest file

Source: R/manifest.R
read_scenarios.Rd

A manifest describes every scenario of a comparison in one YAML file, so the comparison is reproducible from files alone. Each scenario has a name, and either all of its inputs or changes: naming an earlier scenario and only the inputs that differ (layers are merged by name, as in scenario_change()). The first scenario is the baseline.

Usage

read_scenarios(path)

Arguments

path

The manifest file.

Value

A scenario_set().

Details

scenarios:
  - name: Operative
    rulebook: example:exampleton            # or a path to a rulebook file
    parcels: {path: exampleton.gpkg, layer: parcels, filter: {parcel_type: land}}
    roads: {path: exampleton.gpkg, layer: parcels, filter: {parcel_type: road}}
    zoning: {path: exampleton.gpkg, layer: zoning}
    layers:
      height_areas: {path: exampleton.gpkg, layer: height_areas}
  - name: PC1
    changes: Operative
    rulebook: example:exampleton_pc1
    zoning: {path: exampleton_pc1.gpkg, layer: zoning}

A layer is a path to a file sf can read, or a list with path, an optional layer and an optional filter (column to allowed values). Paths are relative to the manifest. Other scenario arguments (such as zone_field, site_id, group_by, street_field, landholding) are given by name.

Examples

set <- read_scenarios(system.file("extdata", "exampleton_pc1_scenarios.yaml", package = "plancap"))
set
#> <plancap scenario set> 2 scenarios; baseline "Operative".
#> PC1 as notified: rulebook, parcels, zoning, layers differ
